precepts.text: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. This rock is Christ himself. I will build my church: the twelve tribes of Israel. So although Britain forbade us to march, trying to hinder black excellence, hinder black unity, hinder the twelve tribes of Israel growing, Christ said the gates of hell will not prevail.
precepts.point: For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids.
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “The Lord of hosts shall defend them”, and “the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” He is not saving all nations; he is only saving the twelve tribes. Christ says the same of his people: “And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

This rock is Christ himself. “I will build my church”: the church is the twelve tribes of Israel. And “the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

So although Britain forbade us to march, trying to hinder black excellence, hinder black unity, hinder the twelve tribes of Israel growing, Christ said the gates of hell will not prevail. They delayed the men's conference, but it still went on, and the presentations were still done. Bishops, deacons, captains, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds all know what the leadership knows, so if one is taken up there are thousands of other men who know exactly the same thing. This will not be stopped.

That is how the Lord defends them. He bends Judah as his bow, fills the bow with Ephraim, and raises up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece, Esau, Edom, the so-called white man, making us as the sword of a mighty man. His arrow goes forth as the lightning, he goes with the whirlwinds of the south, the chariots of God, and we devour and subdue with sling stones. The church he builds on the rock cannot be stopped.

precepts.text: From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. He was talking about raising up himself the third day: Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us.
precepts.point: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?
precepts.why:
This is what he actually said: “From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.” He was talking about raising up himself the third day. Christ's body was the temple.

And his temple today is us. Peter says, “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.” That's the real temple: wherever our people are gathered is a spiritual house. Lively means the laws percolate within us, with zeal, passion and fire, not a boring spirit. Paul says, “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: stones have to come together, so play your position and don't try to change it through deceit. And “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” “for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are”.

How does that temple grow? “Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. Everybody forgets verse one: you have to put away malice, deceit, jealousies and murmuring first. The sincere milk of the word is the law, and we have to drink it like a baby drinks milk, not once a month or once a week, but constantly. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves and our communications: we are the temple.

precepts.text: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. They were hypocrites.
precepts.point: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” What was the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Matthew 23 shows the first part of it.

“The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” They were hypocrites. What they said out of Moses' seat was the law, and that you do. But their works did not match their words.

“Do not ye after their works”, because their works were after someone else, and that is the rest of the leaven: who their works followed. The Passover reminds us that we were delivered because we were unleavened, righteous; so to be delivered again we have to move in the same spirit and purge the leaven out, not just check the box on the physical bread.

precepts.text: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod: letting you know whose manner they were following. They were not just hypocrites; they were following after the manner of the wicked.
precepts.point: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Christ warned in Matthew 16 to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and in Matthew 23 he said to do what they bid from Moses' seat, but not after their works. Whose works were they following? Mark tells it: “And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.”

The leaven of Herod. That lets you know whose manner they were following: they were following the white man, Esau. That is why he tells us to beware.

So their leaven was not just being hypocrites. They were following after the manner of the wicked. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and when the rulers of Israel took on Herod's leaven, it spread through them; they came to move in the same spirit as the wicked they served. That is the warning to us: do not take on the leaven of Herod, the spirit of Esau, while wearing the garments of Israel.

precepts.text: Many of the Jews believed on him, but some went their way to the Pharisees: wherever there is good, evil has to be there. If we let him alone, all men will believe on him, and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation: that lets you know who their masters were. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and that bitterness is on the inside and corrupts the spirit.
precepts.point: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
John 11 shows the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod at work. “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They believed on Christ.

“But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” Wherever there is good, evil has to be there. You had the believers, and then you had coons set up there, running to tell.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans. That lets you know who their masters were and who they were following after. That is the leaven of Herod.

Leaven is an influence that spreads. That bitterness is on the inside, and it corrupts the spirit, the same bitterness that was in Cain toward Abel. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead to keep their place under Rome. If you are bitter toward your brother, you are in the same position as the scribes and Pharisees: the same spirit.

precepts.text: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees. The leaven of the Pharisees was hypocrisy; the leaven of the Pharisees is sin. When you keep reading it says, for they say and do not. So the leaven in the scriptures is really going into sin. The days of unleavened bread that we are celebrating right now represent us being without sin.
precepts.point: Offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel. We were offering our offerings of thanksgiving with leaven, meaning with sin, and thinking that is acceptable to God. You cannot give God offerings while you are in the midst of sin. The Lord said, I do not deal with that.
precepts.why:
Amos rebukes Israel: “offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel”. Christ shows what that leaven is: “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees”.

The leaven of the Pharisees was hypocrisy; the leaven of the Pharisees is sin. Christ is saying, be careful of the sins of the Pharisees, for they say and do not. So the leaven in the scriptures is really going into sin, and leaven is not only bread with yeast in it; it is something much more symbolic.

That is what Amos exposes. We were offering our thanksgiving with leaven, with sin, and thinking that was acceptable to God. You cannot be in the midst of sin and give God thanks offerings. The Lord said, I don't work with that, I don't deal with that. That's how you black people is: in the midst of sin and coming to me with offerings.

So the days of unleavened bread we are celebrating represent us being without sin. The soul that has leaven in it for those seven days is cut off, and that is damnation. It is going into something much heavier: the days of unleavened bread are us fixing ourselves right now, getting rid of the leaven, the sins you are battling, trying to become a better person, so that when the Lord returns our souls are not cut off.

precepts.text: When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped; he just left for a season and came back in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came back by jumping on Peter.
precepts.point: Satan comes for all of us. He comes different ways to defile us and destroy us: for some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. Satan only comes at you at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what I need to strengthen, because that is what Satan is going to try to destroy me with. The worst brothers and sisters are the ones that say they have no weakness, that they are perfect; those are the ones dealing with the heaviest demons and just hiding it. Everybody has weakness. The Lord told Paul, my strength is made perfect in weakness; Paul asked three times for his weakness to be removed, and the Lord said no, fight it and become strong.
precepts.why:
Christ told the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and be raised again the third day. That was a good thing: he had to die to redeem the nation of Israel. But Peter took him and rebuked him: “Be it far from thee, Lord”. And Christ turned and said, “Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me”. What happened there? Satan literally jumped on Peter. That was not Peter; that was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was talking to Satan.

Luke shows how that could be. After the temptation in the wilderness: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” For a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped. He just left for a season and kept coming in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came by jumping on Peter.

That is why Christ told Peter in another place that Satan desired to have him, to sift him as wheat, but that he had prayed for him that his faith fail not.

Satan comes for all of us; that is his job. For some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. He comes at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what you need to strengthen, because that is what Satan will try to destroy you with. The worst are the ones who say they have no weakness; they deal with the heaviest demons and are just good at hiding it. The war is in your mind: when the evil thought comes, rebuke it, as Christ did: get thee behind me.

precepts.text: Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona; thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church. Great leaders empower others and make you believe in yourself, which is how the Bishop raises up bishops, deacons, captains, and soldiers by the thousands.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Christ answered Peter, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then he told him, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

How do you think that made Peter feel? Christ telling you, I am going to build my church upon you. That is what great leaders do. Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in you. They empower others, they strengthen others, they make you believe in yourself and not in them.

That is how a leader transfers his belief onto others, the faith Hebrews 13:7 tells us to follow. It is how the Bishop is able to raise up other bishops, raise up deacons, raise up captains, and soldiers by the thousands. Great leaders raise up more leaders.

precepts.text: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees; the disciples thought he meant bread, but he meant their doctrine, their say-and-do-not hypocrisy. They were Israelites. When leaders warn you of leaven, listen; when you see a spirit on someone who can influence you negatively, consider the end of their conversation, Hebrews 13:7.
precepts.point: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened. Leaven grows.
precepts.why:
“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” Christ was warning the twelve of the leaven. Christ was the leader, and when leaders try to warn you of leaven, you need to listen. He knew what he was talking about.

The disciples “reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.” No, he was not talking about bread. He reminded them of “the five loaves of the five thousand” and “the seven loaves of the four thousand”: it's not about the bread, pay attention. They couldn't receive it at that time, until “Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” The leaven is their doctrine and their sinful nature. Don't get caught up in the things they do: they say and do not, they are hypocrites.

And the Pharisees and the Sadducees were Israelites. That doesn't mean we have anything against anybody, but when you see a spirit on someone who can influence you negatively, beware. It's up to you to listen, but the best thing is to follow, listen and consider the end of their conversation. Be very, very mindful.

precepts.text: What is a man profited if he shall gain the whole world and lose his own soul? To get the fame and fortune our people want, you must sell your soul to these people. LeBron takes care of friends and family but is not allowed to help his people on a major level; that is hush money.
precepts.point: Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God, I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations, the terrorist nations, and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom; thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas. Their military gets wiped out at sea, and it will take time.
precepts.why:
The prince of Tyrus has “gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”, and our people try to get involved in America's wealth, America's riches. They want a piece of the pie. But getting a piece of America's pie is dangerous. Christ asks the question: “For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”

In order to get the fame and fortune that many of our people so desperately want, because we want to take care of our friends and family, you have to sell your soul. You must give your soul to these people.

That is often called hush money. Someone as wealthy as LeBron James takes care of his friends, which is admirable, and his family, which is admirable. But in terms of helping his people on a major level, he is not allowed to do that. That is hush money: hush the F up, and just take care of your friends and family. Oprah, all these people; many of them have gone to Epstein's Island, and their names are on the list.

So the riches of the man who says “I am a God” are not a blessing to reach for. Whoever gains his world gets it by trading away his soul, and the Lord has already said he will bring the terrible of the nations upon that man and bring him down to the pit.

precepts.text: Peter rebuked him, be it far from thee, Lord, and Christ said, get thee behind me, Satan, thou savourest not the things that be of God. Peter had good intentions, but even when good is present evil is there, and Christ spotted Satan from a distance without Peter knowing. Measure your intentions and words through the word of God, because Satan can whisper through your thoughts if your mind is not in tune with the scriptures.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

precepts.text: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; upon this rock, Christ himself, I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. They murdered Nat Turner, Denmark Vesey, and Gabriel Prosser, men who knew they were Israelites, and through whispers and hushes the word kept going. Get the proper understanding of the word and it cannot be stopped.
precepts.point: Be preemptive with the Christians who run to Exodus 12:38, the mixed multitude, to say other nations were part of the church. Leviticus 25:45-46: of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you shall ye buy, and they shall be your bondmen for ever. The mixed multitude were our slaves.
precepts.why:
Christ asks, “But whom say ye that I am?” and Peter answers, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Christ tells him “flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.”

Then verse 18 is the key: “upon this rock I will build my church”. That rock is Christ himself, not Peter. And the church he builds is the same government we read of in Isaiah 9, the same church in the wilderness in Acts 7:38: Israel.

“And the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” There is no stopping us. Once you get the proper understanding of the word of God, you cannot stop it; it is going to flourish and grow. The gates of hell will attempt to stop it, but they will not prevail. They attempted it when they murdered Nat Turner, Denmark Vesey and Gabriel Prosser, men who knew they were Israelites. They said kill them, and it did not stop. Through whispers and hushes, this word kept going.

The gates of hell are not a flesh and blood enemy: “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” In our carnal mind we think that if we organize we can overthrow the system, but we cannot. The governments of this earth are set up by Satan, and God allows it. Only God can bring all that down, and Christ has promised that none of it will prevail against his church.

precepts.text: Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; that confession means something.
precepts.point: Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.
precepts.why:
The confession Christ wants before men is Peter's. When Christ asked, “Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?” they answered, “Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.” Then he asked, “But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

That confession means something. Whoever confesses him before men, he confesses before his Father. Abram was called out alone from his country and kindred; confessing Christ before men, even against your own household, is the same going out.

precepts.text: Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ was not revealed by flesh and blood but by the Father; understanding of the Messiah must be given.
precepts.point: David himself did not ascend, but said the Most High told his Lord to sit at his right hand until his foes are made his footstool, another prophecy pointing to Christ.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Christ asked his disciples, “Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?” Men had all kinds of answers: John the Baptist, Elias, Jeremias, one of the prophets. Then Peter answered, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

Christ told him how he knew: “flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Understanding has to be opened for a man to know that Christ is the Messiah. It is given by the Father, which is why not everyone grasped it.

That is the same Peter now standing up as a witness that this Jesus the Most High raised up and exalted to his right hand. He knows it because it was revealed to him.

precepts.text: Flesh and blood did not reveal Christ to Peter, but the Father, because only the Most High could give understanding already placed in him to receive.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
“Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Flesh and blood did not reveal Christ to Peter; the Father did, because only the Most High could give understanding already placed in him to receive.

It was the same with Saul. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel, but it took the Father revealing his Son in him for everything to make sense, and then he confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
He has the keys of hell and of death. “And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.” People read that and get confused; John 20:23 explains exactly what it means.

You think you are going to do evil and get away with it? You are not getting away. You are going to join with the oppressor against the sons and daughters of God Almighty and think your sins are forgiven? Oh no. You better ask Judas Iscariot about that thing. Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth, meaning whatever sins are retained, as John says, shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, meaning remitted, shall be loosed in heaven: forgiven or not forgiven. That is the power Christ gave to the leadership. Whether you accept it or believe it or not, it is what it is. It has to pertain to somebody. Who is it, TD Jakes, Creflo, Juanita Bynum? It has to be somebody in the Israelite community.

points: The first thing wives say about submission is, as unto the Lord, and you are not Christ; Jesus would not say what you are saying. Really? Peter took him and began to rebuke him, and he turned and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan. Peter was called Satan himself. What is worse than being called Satan? Nobody wants to admit to being rightfully called something. Not that we should be calling each other out of our names, but there are times you need to realize what spirit you are carrying, and that is what Christ did: I see the spirit on you and I am going to tell you what it is.

When did the beginning of sorrows start? Christ told the Pharisees and Sadducees: when it is evening, ye say it will be fair weather, for the sky is red; and in the morning, foul weather today, for the sky is red and lowring. You go outside, look at the sky, and you can tell it is going to rain today.

O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times? We must be able to discern the signs of the times. The Most High gave us signs to look for so we would know what time we are living in. If you are able to look at the signs of the sky and read them, you should be able to watch the signs of the time and read that also.

Y'all know Jake always think they meteorologists. He said, when it's evening, you look up, you say, it's going to be fair weather tomorrow. Y'all know Jake from the hood, we don't know how to look at clouds and red clouds; we just open the window, we stick our hand out, we say, yeah, it's going to be nice today.

O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky, but can ye not discern the signs of the times? We all should be able to discern the signs of the times. You can predict the weather, but you can't line up what's going on. You don't see what time we living in. You don't see that we in the latter days. You don't see prophecy being fulfilled.

Upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. The church is the body of Christ, the twelve tribes. The gates of hell Christ was speaking of at that time was Rome.

What is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? America sold you a dream, and a lot of us came here seeking that dream; a lot have sold their soul for the American dream. That is what Revelation 18 means when she trades slaves and souls of men.

You gain the nice house, the nice job, all these things, but you had to break God's laws to obtain them, so you lost your soul. You agree with the homosexuality, the fornication, all the sins of America; you follow the white man and his religions. That is how America sells souls: I can make you rich, but you have to agree with what I do.
Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
